treaty_name: Convention between the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and the Republic of Bulgaria for the avoidance of double taxation with respect to taxes on income and the prevention of tax evasion (2017)
source_title: ZATCA: SA-BG Convention 2017 with Protocol (English text, Art. 10-12, 26, 28, 29)

rates.quote: However, such dividends may also be taxed in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident and according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the dividends.

However, such income from debt-claims may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which it arises and according to the laws of that Contracting State, but if the beneficial owner of that income is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed 5 per cent of the gross amount of the income from debt-claims.

However, such royalties may also be taxed in the Contracting State in which they arise and according to the laws of that Contracting State, but if the beneficial owner of the royalties is a resident of the other Contracting State, the tax so charged shall not exceed: [...] d) 10 per cent of the gross amount of the royalties in all other cases.

ppt.basis: treaty art. 28(2); MLI art. 7(1) from 2023-01-01 (both Parties notified Art. 28(2) under MLI Art. 7(17)(a))
ppt.quote: Notwithstanding the other provisions of this Convention, a benefit under this Convention shall not be granted in respect of an item of income if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit.

notes: Royalties Art. 12(2)(c) (labelled c in the ZATCA text): 5% for the use of, or right to use, industrial, commercial or scientific equipment - not modelled as a separate tier (general 10% kept). Art. 26: dividends and interest derived by the Government of a Contracting State taxable only in that State (Protocol 4 lists BNB, Bulgarian Development Bank, SAMA, Saudi Fund for Development, PIF, Public Pension Agency, GOSI, wholly owned entities). Protocol 3: interest paid to a pension fund of the other State taxable only in residence State. Protocol 2(b): branch profits tax max 5%. Art. 29(2)(a): WHT provisions apply to amounts paid on or after 1 January next following EIF. EIF CONFLICT: NRA list and Bulgaria MLI list give 01-10-2018; ZATCA page says 'entered into force on 1/11/2018'; Saudi MLI position lists 01-01-2019. Any 2018 date gives WHT effect 2019-01-01; if EIF were 2019-01-01, WHT effect would be 2020-01-01. Saudi Arabia reserved MLI Art. 8 entirely. MLI PPT WHT effective date (2023-01-01) reused from treaty map.
unverified: EIF date conflict between NRA (2018-10-01), ZATCA (2018-11-01) and SA MLI position (2019-01-01)
